notes: SDSS J013655.91+242546.0: eligible as follow_up because §8.4 explicitly covers the five named miscellaneous high-velocity stars as previously identified possible HVSs or hyper-runaways (T:p37-b4); the paper later favors a disk runaway (T:p38-b1), which does not remove follow_up status. HIP 60350: same prior-candidate basis (T:p37-b4); the present paper's origin preference is not used as a new unbound-candidate claim. HE0437-5439: same prior-candidate basis (T:p37-b4), with HVS models favored at T:p38-b2; the paper gives no explicit present-day bound/unbound verdict, so follow_up is used rather than candidates_found. HD 271791: same prior-candidate basis (T:p37-b4), later favored as a disk runaway (T:p38-b1), retained under follow_up. J091206.52+091621.8: same prior-candidate basis (T:p37-b4), with HVS models favored but proper-motion errors noted as preventing isolation of a GC ejection (T:p38-b2). Unnamed samples (the SEGUE HVS candidates, Brown et al. B-type HVS candidates, Silva & Napiwotzki runaways, and BHB/RR Lyrae halo stars) are not entered as individual stars because no per-star identifiers are supplied (T:p33-b1; T:p33-b2; T:p33-b3; T:p34-b1). HVS-1 is only a comparison object (T:p38-b2), and EC 09452-1403 is a named bona-fide runaway not identified as a Galactic unbound candidate (T:p37-b1).

SDSS J013655.91+242546.0: The paper gives only approximate distance and radial velocity for SDSS J013655.91+242546.0 in §8.4 (T:p33-b4); it does not report an explicit equatorial position, parallax, proper-motion value, Galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for this star.

HIP 60350: The paper provides no numerical equatorial coordinates, parallax, or proper-motion components for HIP 60350. Its proper-motion discussion is qualitative: it states that the HVS model predicts a much larger proper motion than observed and that proper motions favor a disk ejection (T:p38-b1).

HE0437-5439: The paper gives only distance and radial velocity for HE0437-5439 at T:p33-b4; no equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motion, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound probability are reported for this star.

HD 271791: HD 271791 is discussed at T:p33-b4 and T:p34-b0 as an 11 M⊙ B-type main-sequence star with d ≈ 21 kpc and v_r ≈ 440 km/s (Heber et al. 2008). At T:p38-b1 the paper states that its observed proper-motion magnitude is much larger than predicted by the simple HVS model, but no numerical proper-motion components are given. No right ascension, declination, parallax, Galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star in the supplied material.

J091206.52+091621.8: Target J091206.52+091621.8 is discussed in T:p34-b0 as a miscellaneous high-velocity star. T:p38-b2 states only that its observed total proper motion is comparable to or less than a predicted roughly 3 milliarcsec yr−1 and that its proper-motion errors are large; no measured equatorial proper-motion components are given. No values were calculated or converted.
